title: [30/09/2025] African telephone subscriber growth 1994-2004
prompt: The graph below gives information about telephone subscribers per 100 inhabitants in Africa from 1994-2004. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph compares the number of telephone subscribers per 100 inhabitants in Africa between 1994 and 2004 for fixed-line and mobile connections.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while access expanded across the decade, growth was driven mainly by mobiles. Notably, mobile subscriptions overtook fixed lines around 2001 and finished the period far ahead, whereas fixed-line penetration rose slowly and remained low.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking first at fixed telephony, subscription levels were about 1.7 per 100 in the mid-1990s and then increased steadily, moving above two by 1997 and reaching roughly 2.2 in 1998. Subsequently, they climbed to around 2.5 in 1999 and 3 per 100 in 2001, before a brief dip in 2002. In the following years towards the end of the period shown, fixed lines recovered slowly to 3.1 per 100 inhabitants in 2004, which was barely double the starting point and thus suggests constraints in traditional networks.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: By contrast, mobile phones began from a negligible base, well below 0.1 per 100, and remained subdued until the turn of the millennium. From 1999 onward, uptake accelerated, in which penetration reached one per 100 that year and then doubled to two in 2000. In 2001, mobiles matched and then surpassed fixed lines at about three subscribers per 100, before rapidly rising to nearly five in 2002, six in 2003, and close to nine per 100 inhabitants by 2004. At the end of the period, mobile penetration was almost three times that of fixed lines, underscoring a decisive shift toward wireless connectivity.
